Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Minnesota debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

Minnesota Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a Minnesota debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the Minnesota Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 395 bankruptcy cases from Minnesota's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 737999.7%0.3%

Chapter 1316n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Bankruptcy Helps Minnesota Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Minnesota debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Minnesota debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Minnesota Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

## Student Loan Default in Mississippi [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing
Source: https://studentloandefault.org/states/mississippi.html

← studentloandefault.org home

Student Loan Default in Mississippi [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Mississippi residents.

Default Consequences in Mississippi

Federal student loans enter default after 270 days of non-payment (for Direct and FFEL loans in repayment). Once in default, the Department of Education can pursue several collection tools without a court judgment - that is the key difference from commercial debt. This page maps how federal default tools intersect with Mississippi law.

If you are a Mississippi resident in default, the five main exposure points are: federal wage garnishment, Treasury Offset Program, professional-license concerns, state wage-garnishment law, and credit reporting.

Federal Administrative Wage Garnishment (AWG) - 15% Cap

Under 20 U.S.C. Section 1095a, the Department of Education may garnish up to 15% of disposable pay without a court order once federal student loans are in default. The garnishment is administrative - no judge, no lawsuit - but you have rights:

30-day notice. ED must send written notice at least 30 days before garnishment begins.

Hearing right. You can request a hearing to challenge the debt's existence or amount, or to assert financial hardship.

Hardship defense. If 15% would create undue hardship, the garnishment amount can be reduced (rarely eliminated).

Rehabilitation stops AWG. Nine qualifying monthly payments under a rehabilitation agreement halt garnishment and remove the default.

Consolidation stops AWG. Consolidating into a new Direct Loan with an IDR plan stops garnishment but does not remove the default notation from your credit report (rehabilitation does both).

The 15% federal cap preempts conflicting state law under the Higher Education Act. Even in states like Texas, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania that broadly prohibit wage garnishment for consumer debt, federal student-loan garnishment still applies.

Mississippi State Wage Garnishment Overlay

Miss. Code 85-3-4: garnishment capped.

State law matters if (1) you have private student loans and the holder has sued you in state court, or (2) a state-court judgment has been entered for collection costs. For private loans, Mississippi garnishment caps control. See private loan default.

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) - Tax Refunds and Federal Payments

The Treasury Offset Program (31 U.S.C. Section 3716) lets the Treasury intercept federal payments owed to a defaulted borrower and apply them to the loan. Intercepted payments include:

Federal income tax refunds (the big one).

Social Security retirement and disability benefits - subject to the $750/month floor under 31 U.S.C. Section 3716(c)(3)(A)(ii) and the 15% cap above that floor.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by Mississippi tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in Mississippi

Mississippi statute historically permitted suspension; current enforcement unclear post-federal preemption.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in Mississippi before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of Mississippi Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For Mississippi debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

Mississippi Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Mississippi Center for Justice.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Mississippi debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

When Bankruptcy Helps Mississippi Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Mississippi debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Mississippi debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Mississippi Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

Professional Licensing in Nevada

No automatic license suspension.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in Nevada before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of Nevada Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For Nevada debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

Nevada Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Nevada debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

Nevada Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a Nevada debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the Nevada Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 242 bankruptcy cases from Nevada's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 716493.4%5.9%

Chapter 137837.2%62.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Bankruptcy Helps Nevada Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Nevada debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Nevada debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Nevada Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

## Student Loan Default in New Hampshire [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing
Source: https://studentloandefault.org/states/new-hampshire.html

← studentloandefault.org home

Student Loan Default in New Hampshire [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New Hampshire residents.

Default Consequences in New Hampshire

Federal student loans enter default after 270 days of non-payment (for Direct and FFEL loans in repayment). Once in default, the Department of Education can pursue several collection tools without a court judgment - that is the key difference from commercial debt. This page maps how federal default tools intersect with New Hampshire law.

If you are a New Hampshire resident in default, the five main exposure points are: federal wage garnishment, Treasury Offset Program, professional-license concerns, state wage-garnishment law, and credit reporting.

Federal Administrative Wage Garnishment (AWG) - 15% Cap

Under 20 U.S.C. Section 1095a, the Department of Education may garnish up to 15% of disposable pay without a court order once federal student loans are in default. The garnishment is administrative - no judge, no lawsuit - but you have rights:

30-day notice. ED must send written notice at least 30 days before garnishment begins.

Hearing right. You can request a hearing to challenge the debt's existence or amount, or to assert financial hardship.

Hardship defense. If 15% would create undue hardship, the garnishment amount can be reduced (rarely eliminated).

Rehabilitation stops AWG. Nine qualifying monthly payments under a rehabilitation agreement halt garnishment and remove the default.

Consolidation stops AWG. Consolidating into a new Direct Loan with an IDR plan stops garnishment but does not remove the default notation from your credit report (rehabilitation does both).

The 15% federal cap preempts conflicting state law under the Higher Education Act. Even in states like Texas, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania that broadly prohibit wage garnishment for consumer debt, federal student-loan garnishment still applies.

New Hampshire State Wage Garnishment Overlay

RSA 512:21: garnishment capped.

State law matters if (1) you have private student loans and the holder has sued you in state court, or (2) a state-court judgment has been entered for collection costs. For private loans, New Hampshire garnishment caps control. See private loan default.

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) - Tax Refunds and Federal Payments

The Treasury Offset Program (31 U.S.C. Section 3716) lets the Treasury intercept federal payments owed to a defaulted borrower and apply them to the loan. Intercepted payments include:

Federal income tax refunds (the big one).

Social Security retirement and disability benefits - subject to the $750/month floor under 31 U.S.C. Section 3716(c)(3)(A)(ii) and the 15% cap above that floor.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by New Hampshire tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in New Hampshire

No license suspension for default.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in New Hampshire before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of New Hampshire Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For New Hampshire debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

New Hampshire Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

New Hampshire Legal Assistance.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A New Hampshire debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See New Hampshire Brunner test application.

Under 20 U.S.C. Section 1095a, the Department of Education may garnish up to 15% of disposable pay without a court order once federal student loans are in default. The garnishment is administrative - no judge, no lawsuit - but you have rights:

30-day notice. ED must send written notice at least 30 days before garnishment begins.

Hearing right. You can request a hearing to challenge the debt's existence or amount, or to assert financial hardship.

Hardship defense. If 15% would create undue hardship, the garnishment amount can be reduced (rarely eliminated).

Rehabilitation stops AWG. Nine qualifying monthly payments under a rehabilitation agreement halt garnishment and remove the default.

Consolidation stops AWG. Consolidating into a new Direct Loan with an IDR plan stops garnishment but does not remove the default notation from your credit report (rehabilitation does both).

The 15% federal cap preempts conflicting state law under the Higher Education Act. Even in states like Texas, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania that broadly prohibit wage garnishment for consumer debt, federal student-loan garnishment still applies.

North Carolina State Wage Garnishment Overlay

N.C.G.S. 1-362: garnishment limited to taxes and child support primarily; federal ED still offsets.

State law matters if (1) you have private student loans and the holder has sued you in state court, or (2) a state-court judgment has been entered for collection costs. For private loans, North Carolina garnishment caps control. See private loan default.

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) - Tax Refunds and Federal Payments

The Treasury Offset Program (31 U.S.C. Section 3716) lets the Treasury intercept federal payments owed to a defaulted borrower and apply them to the loan. Intercepted payments include:

Federal income tax refunds (the big one).

Social Security retirement and disability benefits - subject to the $750/month floor under 31 U.S.C. Section 3716(c)(3)(A)(ii) and the 15% cap above that floor.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by North Carolina tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in North Carolina

NC historically had license suspension but repealed / narrowed the provision; current enforcement minimal.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in North Carolina before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of North Carolina Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For North Carolina debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

North Carolina Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Legal Aid of North Carolina.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A North Carolina debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

North Carolina Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a North Carolina debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the North Carolina Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 827 bankruptcy cases from North Carolina's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7273n/an/a

Chapter 13554n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Bankruptcy Helps North Carolina Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted North Carolina debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A North Carolina debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See North Carolina Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

## Student Loan Default in Pennsylvania [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing
Source: https://studentloandefault.org/states/pennsylvania.html

← studentloandefault.org home

Student Loan Default in Pennsylvania [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Pennsylvania residents.

Default Consequences in Pennsylvania

Federal student loans enter default after 270 days of non-payment (for Direct and FFEL loans in repayment). Once in default, the Department of Education can pursue several collection tools without a court judgment - that is the key difference from commercial debt. This page maps how federal default tools intersect with Pennsylvania law.

If you are a Pennsylvania resident in default, the five main exposure points are: federal wage garnishment, Treasury Offset Program, professional-license concerns, state wage-garnishment law, and credit reporting.

Federal Administrative Wage Garnishment (AWG) - 15% Cap

Under 20 U.S.C. Section 1095a, the Department of Education may garnish up to 15% of disposable pay without a court order once federal student loans are in default. The garnishment is administrative - no judge, no lawsuit - but you have rights:

30-day notice. ED must send written notice at least 30 days before garnishment begins.

Hearing right. You can request a hearing to challenge the debt's existence or amount, or to assert financial hardship.

Hardship defense. If 15% would create undue hardship, the garnishment amount can be reduced (rarely eliminated).

Rehabilitation stops AWG. Nine qualifying monthly payments under a rehabilitation agreement halt garnishment and remove the default.

Consolidation stops AWG. Consolidating into a new Direct Loan with an IDR plan stops garnishment but does not remove the default notation from your credit report (rehabilitation does both).

The 15% federal cap preempts conflicting state law under the Higher Education Act. Even in states like Texas, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania that broadly prohibit wage garnishment for consumer debt, federal student-loan garnishment still applies.

Pennsylvania State Wage Garnishment Overlay

42 Pa.C.S. Section 8127: PA generally prohibits wage garnishment for most consumer debts; federal ED 15% still applies to federal loans via HEA preemption.

State law matters if (1) you have private student loans and the holder has sued you in state court, or (2) a state-court judgment has been entered for collection costs. For private loans, Pennsylvania garnishment caps control. See private loan default.

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) - Tax Refunds and Federal Payments

The Treasury Offset Program (31 U.S.C. Section 3716) lets the Treasury intercept federal payments owed to a defaulted borrower and apply them to the loan. Intercepted payments include:

Federal income tax refunds (the big one).

Social Security retirement and disability benefits - subject to the $750/month floor under 31 U.S.C. Section 3716(c)(3)(A)(ii) and the 15% cap above that floor.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by Pennsylvania tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in Pennsylvania

No license suspension for federal student loan default.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in Pennsylvania before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of Pennsylvania Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For Pennsylvania debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

Pennsylvania Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Community Legal Services of Philadelphia; MidPenn Legal Services.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Pennsylvania debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

Pennsylvania Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a Pennsylvania debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the Pennsylvania Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,513 bankruptcy cases from Pennsylvania's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7415n/an/a

Chapter 131,098n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Bankruptcy Helps Pennsylvania Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Pennsylvania debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Pennsylvania debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Pennsylvania Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

Loan rehabilitation

Consolidation after default

Credit impact

Pennsylvania Brunner test

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Tennessee debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

Tennessee Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a Tennessee debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the Tennessee Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,840 bankruptcy cases from Tennessee's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 758995.5%4.5%

Chapter 131,25117.3%82.7%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Bankruptcy Helps Tennessee Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Tennessee debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Tennessee debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Tennessee Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

## Student Loan Default in Texas [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing
Source: https://studentloandefault.org/states/texas.html

← studentloandefault.org home

Student Loan Default in Texas [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Texas residents.

Default Consequences in Texas

Federal student loans enter default after 270 days of non-payment (for Direct and FFEL loans in repayment). Once in default, the Department of Education can pursue several collection tools without a court judgment - that is the key difference from commercial debt. This page maps how federal default tools intersect with Texas law.

If you are a Texas resident in default, the five main exposure points are: federal wage garnishment, Treasury Offset Program, professional-license concerns, state wage-garnishment law, and credit reporting.

Federal Administrative Wage Garnishment (AWG) - 15% Cap

Under 20 U.S.C. Section 1095a, the Department of Education may garnish up to 15% of disposable pay without a court order once federal student loans are in default. The garnishment is administrative - no judge, no lawsuit - but you have rights:

30-day notice. ED must send written notice at least 30 days before garnishment begins.

Hearing right. You can request a hearing to challenge the debt's existence or amount, or to assert financial hardship.

Hardship defense. If 15% would create undue hardship, the garnishment amount can be reduced (rarely eliminated).

Rehabilitation stops AWG. Nine qualifying monthly payments under a rehabilitation agreement halt garnishment and remove the default.

Consolidation stops AWG. Consolidating into a new Direct Loan with an IDR plan stops garnishment but does not remove the default notation from your credit report (rehabilitation does both).

The 15% federal cap preempts conflicting state law under the Higher Education Act. Even in states like Texas, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania that broadly prohibit wage garnishment for consumer debt, federal student-loan garnishment still applies.

Texas State Wage Garnishment Overlay

Tex. Const. art. XVI s.28: strong wage-protection; federal ED offsets and Treasury offsets apply regardless.

State law matters if (1) you have private student loans and the holder has sued you in state court, or (2) a state-court judgment has been entered for collection costs. For private loans, Texas garnishment caps control. See private loan default.

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) - Tax Refunds and Federal Payments

The Treasury Offset Program (31 U.S.C. Section 3716) lets the Treasury intercept federal payments owed to a defaulted borrower and apply them to the loan. Intercepted payments include:

Federal income tax refunds (the big one).

Social Security retirement and disability benefits - subject to the $750/month floor under 31 U.S.C. Section 3716(c)(3)(A)(ii) and the 15% cap above that floor.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by Texas tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in Texas

Texas generally does NOT allow wage garnishment for consumer debt (state constitutional protection). Federal 15% ED garnishment still applies to federal student loans via HEA preemption.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in Texas before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of Texas Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For Texas debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

Texas Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Texas RioGrande Legal Aid; Lone Star Legal Aid.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Texas debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

Texas Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a Texas debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the Texas Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 30,781 bankruptcy cases from Texas's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711,84497.8%2.0%

Chapter 1318,93736.8%63.2%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Bankruptcy Helps Texas Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Texas debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Texas debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Texas Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by Washington tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in Washington

No license suspension for default.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in Washington before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of Washington Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For Washington debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

Washington Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Northwest Justice Project; Columbia Legal Services.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A Washington debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

When Bankruptcy Helps Washington Defaulted Borrowers

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted Washington debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.

Chapter 13 reorganization. A Washington debtor in Ch 13 pays student-loan arrears through the plan; the stay lasts 3-5 years and allows a post-plan discharge adversary if warranted.

Section 523(a)(8) adversary. If undue hardship applies under the circuit's test (Brunner or totality), student loans themselves can be discharged. See Washington Brunner test application.

See credit impact of default and default timeline.

## Student Loan Default in West Virginia [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing
Source: https://studentloandefault.org/states/west-virginia.html

← studentloandefault.org home

Student Loan Default in West Virginia [2026]: Garnishment, Offset, Licensing

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for West Virginia residents.

Default Consequences in West Virginia

Federal student loans enter default after 270 days of non-payment (for Direct and FFEL loans in repayment). Once in default, the Department of Education can pursue several collection tools without a court judgment - that is the key difference from commercial debt. This page maps how federal default tools intersect with West Virginia law.

If you are a West Virginia resident in default, the five main exposure points are: federal wage garnishment, Treasury Offset Program, professional-license concerns, state wage-garnishment law, and credit reporting.

Federal Administrative Wage Garnishment (AWG) - 15% Cap

Under 20 U.S.C. Section 1095a, the Department of Education may garnish up to 15% of disposable pay without a court order once federal student loans are in default. The garnishment is administrative - no judge, no lawsuit - but you have rights:

30-day notice. ED must send written notice at least 30 days before garnishment begins.

Hearing right. You can request a hearing to challenge the debt's existence or amount, or to assert financial hardship.

Hardship defense. If 15% would create undue hardship, the garnishment amount can be reduced (rarely eliminated).

Rehabilitation stops AWG. Nine qualifying monthly payments under a rehabilitation agreement halt garnishment and remove the default.

Consolidation stops AWG. Consolidating into a new Direct Loan with an IDR plan stops garnishment but does not remove the default notation from your credit report (rehabilitation does both).

The 15% federal cap preempts conflicting state law under the Higher Education Act. Even in states like Texas, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania that broadly prohibit wage garnishment for consumer debt, federal student-loan garnishment still applies.

West Virginia State Wage Garnishment Overlay

W. Va. Code 38-5A-3: garnishment capped.

State law matters if (1) you have private student loans and the holder has sued you in state court, or (2) a state-court judgment has been entered for collection costs. For private loans, West Virginia garnishment caps control. See private loan default.

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) - Tax Refunds and Federal Payments

The Treasury Offset Program (31 U.S.C. Section 3716) lets the Treasury intercept federal payments owed to a defaulted borrower and apply them to the loan. Intercepted payments include:

Federal income tax refunds (the big one).

Social Security retirement and disability benefits - subject to the $750/month floor under 31 U.S.C. Section 3716(c)(3)(A)(ii) and the 15% cap above that floor.

Federal employee salaries (for federal-employee debtors) up to 15%.

Federal contractor payments.

TOP operates nationwide and is not affected by West Virginia tax or income-protection law.

Professional Licensing in West Virginia

No automatic license suspension.

The federal landscape on license suspension for student-loan default has changed dramatically. In the 1990s and 2000s many states statutorily suspended professional licenses for defaulted borrowers. Most of those provisions have been repealed, narrowed, or are no longer enforced after Congress stopped conditioning state aid on them. Always verify with your specific licensing board in West Virginia before assuming your license is at risk.

Federal security clearances also sometimes reference student-loan default; the relevant adjudicative guideline is "financial considerations" (SEAD-4 Guideline F), which weighs default history but rarely results in clearance loss for documented-hardship cases.

Credit Reporting of West Virginia Default

Federal student loan default appears on credit reports as a serious delinquency, with collection activity and TOP/AWG notations. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, default notations remain for 7 years from the original delinquency date (not from default date or collection date). Rehabilitation removes the default notation from the credit report (but not the late-payment history); consolidation does not.

For West Virginia debtors looking to buy a home, an active default blocks FHA, VA, USDA, and most conventional mortgages because these loans pull the CAIVRS federal delinquent-debtor database. See getting out of default.

West Virginia Rehabilitation and Consolidation Resources

Legal Aid of West Virginia.

The two federal paths out of default are:

Loan rehabilitation. 9 qualifying monthly payments at a reasonable-and-affordable amount (can be as low as $5/month on a documented-hardship basis). Removes the default from credit report and restores IDR/PSLF eligibility. One-time-only per loan.

Direct Consolidation. Combine defaulted loans into a new Direct Consolidation Loan with an IDR plan. Faster than rehabilitation but does not remove the default notation from the credit report.

A West Virginia debtor eligible for rehabilitation should almost always prefer rehabilitation over consolidation for the first exit from default. Consolidation is the better choice if rehabilitation has already been used, or if immediate IDR access is more important than credit repair.

West Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

Default drives filings: a West Virginia debtor facing wage garnishment, tax-refund offset, and servicer pressure often turns to bankruptcy. These FJC numbers show the West Virginia Chapter 7 and 13 volume where defaulted-student-loan debtors landed.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 60 bankruptcy cases from West Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

Bankruptcy does not automatically discharge student loans, but it does several useful things for defaulted West Virginia debtors:

Automatic stay. 11 U.S.C. Section 362 halts Administrative Wage Garnishment, Treasury offsets going forward, and state-court private-loan lawsuits immediately on filing.

Clears co-debt. Credit-card debt, medical bills, and most unsecured debt discharge in Chapter 7; this frees cash flow that can then support IDR.
